scope: KB1 Down four-row cold sample, frozen 512-bit writer and strictly serial TB AXI B endpoint; read-only interpretation.
source_rules: TB AWREADY=!aw_seen && cycle%7!=0; WREADY=!w_seen && cycle%11!=0; aw_seen/w_seen clear only on actual B consume.
TB sets bdelay=17+(physical output_beats%3) and decrements once per negedge; BVALID held until BREADY.
Writer has one immutable tx; next sealed pack transfers only when tx empty or actual B fires.
Final PS commit_ready for last group follows final_adapter ready; adapter stored row retires through bias output whose pending output waits writer packet_ready.
judgment: The declared response profile already reaches the minimum 256 physical W beats. The TB serializes all transactions and accounts for 4608 B-delay decrements within the measured 4927-cycle first-AW-to-last-B span. Packet/PS stall counters are overlapping and cannot be converted directly to command savings. A write-buffer change can matter only if it advances first AW or changes another critical overlap; with first AW unchanged, eliminating every non-B output interval could save at most 319 cycles in that interval, and even that is optimistic. A multi-outstanding memory peer is a different response profile requiring its own baseline.
limitations: The 319-cycle quantity is a conditional ceiling for the measured output interval, not total command latency or a realized optimization.
Static readiness chain identifies possible propagation, but existing counters do not measure simultaneous causes or prove exact critical-path attribution.
No physical HBM timing or steady-state throughput evidence.
